questions.question: What is the chemical formula of nitric acid? (FBISE 2024-II)
questions.explanation: Nitric acid has the molecular formula $HNO_3$. It is a strong mineral acid widely used in fertilizer and explosive manufacturing.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds behaves as a Lewis base? (FBISE 2023-II, 2024-I)
questions.explanation: Ammonia ($NH_3$) possesses an unshared lone pair of electrons on its nitrogen atom which it can donate to form a coordinate covalent bond, making it a classic Lewis base.

questions.question: A substance that can donate a proton ($H^+$) to another substance is defined as an acid according to: (FBISE 2023-II)
questions.explanation: In 1923, J.N. Brønsted and T.M. Lowry independently defined an acid as any chemical species capable of donating a proton ($H^+$) to another substance.

questions.question: Which of the following substances is an amphoteric compound capable of acting as both a Brønsted acid and a Brønsted base? (FBISE 2021-I, 2025 Model)
questions.explanation: Water ($H_2O$) is amphoteric: it acts as a Brønsted acid by donating a proton to form hydroxide ($OH^-$), and as a Brønsted base by accepting a proton to form hydronium ($H_3O^+$).

questions.question: Identify the Arrhenius base among the following choices: (FBISE 2025 Model)
questions.explanation: According to the Arrhenius concept, a base is a substance that dissociates in aqueous solution to yield hydroxide ions ($OH^-$). Sodium hydroxide ($NaOH \to Na^+ + OH^-$) is an Arrhenius base.

questions.question: What is the conjugate acid of the bicarbonate ion ($HCO_3^-$)? (FBISE 2022-I)
questions.explanation: A conjugate acid is formed when a base accepts a proton. When $HCO_3^-$ accepts a proton ($H^+$), it forms carbonic acid ($H_2CO_3$).

questions.question: What is the conjugate base of water ($H_2O$)? (FBISE 2019-I)
questions.explanation: When water acts as an acid and donates a proton ($H^+$), the remaining species is the hydroxide ion ($OH^-$), which is its conjugate base.

questions.question: What is the pH of a neutral aqueous solution at $25^\circ\text{C}$? (FBISE 2018-I, 2020-II)
questions.explanation: In pure water at $25^\circ\text{C}$, $[H^+] = 1.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ M}$. Taking the negative logarithm gives $pH = -\log(1.0 \times 10^{-7}) = 7$.

questions.question: If an aqueous solution has a $pOH$ of 4, what is its $pH$ value at $25^\circ\text{C}$? (FBISE 2017-II)
questions.explanation: At $25^\circ\text{C}$, $pH + pOH = 14$. Therefore, $pH = 14 - pOH = 14 - 4 = 10$, indicating a basic solution.

questions.question: What gas is evolved with effervescence when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with calcium carbonate ($CaCO_3$)? (FBISE 2016-I, 2023-I)
questions.explanation: Acids react with metal carbonates and bicarbonates to form salt, water, and liberate carbon dioxide gas: $CaCO_3 + 2HCl \to CaCl_2 + H_2O + CO_2\uparrow$.

questions.question: What gas is liberated when dilute sulphuric acid reacts with active zinc metal? (FBISE 2015-II, 2019-II)
questions.explanation: Metals above hydrogen in the electrochemical series displace hydrogen from dilute non-oxidizing acids: $Zn + H_2SO_4 \to ZnSO_4 + H_2\uparrow$.

questions.question: What gas having a characteristic rotten egg odor is produced when an acid reacts with iron(II) sulphide ($FeS$)? (FBISE 2017-I)
questions.explanation: Acids react with metal sulphides to release toxic hydrogen sulphide gas ($H_2S$), which is well known for its offensive rotten egg smell: $FeS + 2HCl \to FeCl_2 + H_2S\uparrow$.

questions.question: When dilute sodium hydroxide solution is added to a copper sulphate solution, what colored precipitate forms? (FBISE 2018-II, 2022-II)
questions.explanation: Bases precipitate insoluble metal hydroxides from their salt solutions. Copper sulphate reacts with sodium hydroxide to precipitate light blue copper(II) hydroxide: $CuSO_4 + 2NaOH \to Cu(OH)_2\downarrow + Na_2SO_4$.

questions.question: When phenolphthalein indicator is added to a basic solution ($pH > 9$), what color change occurs? (FBISE 2014-I, 2021-II)
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is an organic indicator that is colorless in acidic and neutral solutions ($pH < 8.3$) and turns distinct pink/magenta in alkaline solutions ($pH 8.3 - 10$).

questions.question: Methyl orange indicator produces what color in a strongly acidic solution? (FBISE 2015-I)
questions.explanation: Methyl orange indicator exhibits a red color in acidic solutions ($pH < 3.1$) and turns yellow in alkaline medium ($pH > 4.4$).

questions.question: Which of the following salts is classified as an acidic salt? (FBISE 2020-I, 2023-I)
questions.explanation: An acidic salt is formed by the partial replacement of ionizable hydrogen atoms of a polybasic acid by a metal ion. Sodium bisulphate ($NaHSO_4$) retains an ionizable hydrogen ion.

questions.question: Which of the following salts is a normal (neutral) salt? (FBISE 2019-II)
questions.explanation: A normal salt is formed by the total replacement of ionizable hydrogen atoms of an acid by metal ions. Sodium chloride ($NaCl$) contains no replaceable hydrogen or hydroxyl ions.

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a basic salt? (FBISE 2018-I)
questions.explanation: Basic salts are formed by the incomplete neutralization of a polyhydroxy base by an acid, retaining one or more replaceable hydroxide ($OH^-$) groups, such as $Al(OH)_2Cl$ or $Pb(OH)NO_3$.

questions.question: Potash alum ($K_2SO_4 \cdot Al_2(SO_4)_3 \cdot 24H_2O$) is an example of a: (FBISE 2016-II, 2022-I)
questions.explanation: A double salt is formed by the equimolar crystallization of two simple salts and retains the individual identities of all its constituent ions in solution. Potash alum is a classic double salt.

questions.question: Bleaching powder ($CaOCl_2$) is an example of a: (FBISE 2017-II)
questions.explanation: A mixed salt contains more than one basic or acidic radical. Bleaching powder consists of one cation ($Ca^{2+}$) combined with two different anions ($Cl^-$ and $OCl^-$).

questions.question: What is the numerical value of the auto-ionization constant of water ($K_w$) at $25^\circ\text{C}$? (FBISE 2021-I)
questions.explanation: At $25^\circ\text{C}$, the ionic product of water $K_w = [H^+][OH^-] = (1.0 \times 10^{-7})(1.0 \times 10^{-7}) = 1.0 \times 10^{-14}$.

questions.question: Which method is used to prepare an insoluble salt like barium sulphate ($BaSO_4$)? (FBISE 2019-I, 2023-II)

options.B: Reaction of acid with an insoluble base
options.C: Precipitation by mixing two soluble salt solutions (double decomposition)
options.D: Action of acid on pure metal

questions.explanation: Insoluble salts are prepared by precipitation (ionic double displacement) when solutions of two soluble salts containing the required ions are mixed: $BaCl_2(aq) + Na_2SO_4(aq) \to BaSO_4\downarrow + 2NaCl(aq)$.

questions.question: What is the concentration of hydrogen ions in a solution with a pH of 3?
Which of the following acids is present in sour milk and yogurt?
questions.explanation: Lactic acid is produced by the fermentation of milk sugar (lactose) by Lactobacillus bacteria, giving sour milk and yogurt their distinctive taste.

questions.question: Which acid is found naturally in sting of bees and ants?
questions.explanation: Ants and bees inject formic acid ($HCOOH$, methanoic acid) when they sting, causing burning pain and inflammation.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is an example of an electron-deficient Lewis acid?
questions.explanation: Boron trifluoride ($BF_3$) has only 6 valence electrons around its central boron atom. Being two electrons short of an octet, it readily accepts an electron pair, acting as a Lewis acid.

questions.question: In the reaction $NH_3 + BF_3 \to H_3N \to BF_3$, what type of chemical bond links the donor and acceptor atoms?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen donates its lone pair of electrons to the empty orbital of boron, forming a coordinate covalent (dative) bond in the resulting adduct.

questions.question: Which chemical salt is known commercially as baking soda?
questions.explanation: Sodium hydrogen carbonate ($NaHCO_3$) is widely known as baking soda. Upon heating, it releases $CO_2$ gas which causes dough to rise.

questions.question: Plaster of Paris has which of the following chemical formulas?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate ($CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O$), produced by gently heating gypsum ($CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O$) to 100°C.

questions.question: What is the common chemical name of Epsom salt?
questions.explanation: Magnesium sulphate heptahydrate ($MgSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O$) is known as Epsom salt, frequently used as a laxative and in soaking baths.

questions.question: What is the pH range of a universal indicator paper from strongly acidic to strongly alkaline?
questions.explanation: Universal indicator is a mixture of several dyes that shows distinct color changes over the entire pH spectrum from 0 (strong acid, red) to 14 (strong alkali, violet/purple).

questions.question: Which of the following is a major limitation of the Arrhenius acid-base concept?

options.A: It is applicable only to non-aqueous solvents like benzene
options.B: It is restricted exclusively to aqueous medium and cannot explain basicity of $NH_3$
options.D: It predicts that all acids are gases

questions.explanation: Arrhenius theory applies only to aqueous solutions and fails to explain substances like $NH_3$ (which lacks $OH^-$ but acts as a base) and $CO_2$ or $SO_2$ (which lack $H^+$ but act as acidic).

questions.question: In the reaction $HCl + H_2O \rightleftharpoons H_3O^+ + Cl^-$, which species forms a conjugate acid-base pair?
questions.explanation: $HCl$ donates a proton to become $Cl^-$. Therefore, $HCl$ (acid) and $Cl^-$ (conjugate base) constitute a conjugate acid-base pair differing by exactly one proton.

questions.question: When solid ammonium chloride ($NH_4Cl$) is heated with sodium hydroxide ($NaOH$), what pungent gas is evolved?
questions.explanation: Heating an ammonium salt with an alkali liberates ammonia gas: $NH_4Cl + NaOH \to NaCl + H_2O + NH_3\uparrow$.

questions.question: Which salt is used in the manufacture of glass, soap, and paper?
questions.explanation: Sodium carbonate (soda ash, $Na_2CO_3$) is a vital industrial chemical used as a flux in glass making, in saponification for soaps, and in wood pulp processing for paper.

questions.question: What is the pH of a $0.001\text{ M } HCl$ solution?
questions.explanation: $HCl$ is a strong monoprotic acid that ionizes completely. $[H^+] = 0.001\text{ M} = 10^{-3}\text{ M}$. $pH = -\log(10^{-3}) = 3$.

questions.question: What is the pH of a $0.01\text{ M } NaOH$ solution at $25^\circ\text{C}$?
questions.explanation: $NaOH$ is a strong base that ionizes completely: $[OH^-] = 0.01\text{ M} = 10^{-2}\text{ M}$. $pOH = -\log(10^{-2}) = 2$. $pH = 14 - pOH = 14 - 2 = 12$.

questions.question: Blue vitriol is the common name for which hydrated salt?
questions.explanation: Hydrated copper(II) sulphate ($CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O$) forms bright blue triclinic crystals and is commonly known as blue vitriol.

questions.question: Which of the following oxides is an acidic oxide (acid anhydride)?
questions.explanation: Non-metal oxides like sulphur trioxide ($SO_3$) dissolve in water to produce acids ($SO_3 + H_2O \to H_2SO_4$), making them acidic oxides or acid anhydrides.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is an example of a Lewis acid with an expanded octet or empty d-orbitals?
questions.explanation: Aluminum trichloride ($AlCl_3$) has an incomplete octet (6 valence electrons around aluminum) and readily accepts an electron pair, acting as a powerful Lewis acid in Friedel-Crafts reactions.
